passages.text: If there is a dispute between men, they are to go to court to be judged, so that the innocent may be acquitted and the guilty condemned.
passages.sermon:
Two men may have a dispute.
They must go to court.
The judges will decide the case.
The judges will declare the innocent man righteous.
The judges will declare the guilty man guilty.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶ֥ה רִיב֙ בֵּ֣ין אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְנִגְּשׁ֥וּ אֶל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט וּשְׁפָט֑וּם וְהִצְדִּ֙יקוּ֙ אֶת־ הַצַּדִּ֔יק וְהִרְשִׁ֖יעוּ אֶת־ הָרָשָֽׁע׃

passages.text: If the guilty man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall have him lie down and be flogged in his presence with the number of lashes his crime warrants.
passages.sermon:
A judge decides if a man is guilty.
If the man is guilty, the judge gives him a punishment.
The judge makes the guilty man lie down.
The judge orders that the man be beaten.
The judge watches as the man is beaten.
The number of lashes matches the man’s crime.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֛ה אִם־ בִּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹת הָרָשָׁ֑ע וְהִפִּיל֤וֹ הַשֹּׁפֵט֙ וְהִכָּ֣הוּ לְפָנָ֔יו כְּדֵ֥י רִשְׁעָת֖וֹ בְּמִסְפָּֽר׃

passages.text: He may receive no more than forty lashes, lest your brother be beaten any more than that and be degraded in your sight.
passages.sermon:
A judge may order a guilty man to be beaten.
The judge must not give him more than forty lashes.
If the judge gives more than forty lashes, the punishment becomes too severe.
If the punishment is too severe, your brother will be degraded in your sight.
passages.original: אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יַכֶּ֖נּוּ לֹ֣א יֹסִ֑יף פֶּן־ יֹסִ֨יף לְהַכֹּת֤וֹ עַל־ אֵ֙לֶּה֙ מַכָּ֣ה רַבָּ֔ה וְנִקְלָ֥ה אָחִ֖יךָ לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command about animals.
God said, “Do not muzzle an ox.”
An ox treads out grain.
Do not stop the ox from eating while it works.

passages.text: When brothers dwell together and one of them dies without a son, the widow must not marry outside the family. Her husband’s brother is to take her as his wife and fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law for her.
passages.sermon:
When brothers live together, they share the same household.
If one brother dies and leaves no son, his wife becomes a widow.
The widow must not marry a man from outside the family.
The dead man’s brother must marry the widow.
He must take her as his wife.
He must fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law for her.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יֵשְׁב֨וּ אַחִ֜ים יַחְדָּ֗ו וּמֵ֨ת אַחַ֤ד מֵהֶם֙ וּבֵ֣ן אֵֽין־ ל֔וֹ לֹֽא־ תִהְיֶ֧ה אֵֽשֶׁת־ הַמֵּ֛ת הַח֖וּצָה לְאִ֣ישׁ זָ֑ר יְבָמָהּ֙ יָבֹ֣א עָלֶ֔יהָ וּלְקָחָ֥הּ ל֛וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֖ה וְיִבְּמָֽהּ׃

passages.text: The first son she bears will carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be blotted out from Israel.
passages.sermon:
A woman’s husband has died.
She has no son.
Her husband’s brother marries her.
She gives birth to a son.
This son is the firstborn.
This firstborn son will be named for the dead brother.
The dead brother’s name will continue in Israel.
No one will erase his name from Israel.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה הַבְּכוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּלֵ֔ד יָק֕וּם עַל־ שֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו הַמֵּ֑ת וְלֹֽא־ יִמָּחֶ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: But if the man does not want to marry his brother’s widow, she is to go to the elders at the city gate and say, “My husband’s brother refuses to preserve his brother’s name in Israel. He is not willing to perform the duty of a brother-in-law for me.”
passages.sermon:
A man may have a brother who dies without a son.
The dead brother’s widow needs someone to continue her husband’s family line.
The living brother has a duty to marry the widow and raise children for his brother.
If the man does not want to marry his brother’s widow, he may refuse.
The widow must then go to the elders at the city gate.
She must speak to the elders.
She must say, “My husband’s brother refuses to keep his brother’s name alive in Israel.”
She must say, “He is not willing to do the duty of a brother-in-law for me.”
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֤א יַחְפֹּץ֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ לָקַ֖חַת אֶת־ יְבִמְתּ֑וֹ וְעָלְתָה֩ יְבִמְתּ֨וֹ הַשַּׁ֜עְרָה אֶל־ הַזְּקֵנִ֗ים וְאָֽמְרָה֙ מֵאֵ֨ין יְבָמִ֜י לְהָקִ֨ים לְאָחִ֥יו שֵׁם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה יַבְּמִֽי׃

passages.text: Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak with him. If he persists and says, “I do not want to marry her,” his brother’s widow shall go up to him in the presence of the elders, remove his sandal, spit in his face, and declare, “This is what is done to the man who will not maintain his brother’s line.”
passages.sermon:
The elders of the city call the man.
The elders speak with him.
The man stands before them.
The man says, “I do not want to take her as my wife.”
The dead brother’s widow approaches the man.
She does this in front of the elders.
She removes his sandal from his foot.
She spits in his face.
She says, “This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother’s house.”
passages.original: וְקָֽרְאוּ־ ל֥וֹ זִקְנֵי־ עִיר֖וֹ וְדִבְּר֣וּ אֵלָ֑יו וְעָמַ֣ד וְאָמַ֔ר לֹ֥א חָפַ֖צְתִּי לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃ וְנִגְּשָׁ֨ה יְבִמְתּ֣וֹ אֵלָיו֮ לְעֵינֵ֣י הַזְּקֵנִים֒ וְחָלְצָ֤ה נַעֲלוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְל֔וֹ וְיָרְקָ֖ה בְּפָנָ֑יו וְעָֽנְתָה֙ וְאָ֣מְרָ֔ה כָּ֚כָה יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה לָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ יִבְנֶ֖ה אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית אָחִֽיו

passages.text: And his family name in Israel will be called “The House of the Unsandaled.”
passages.sermon: The people of Israel will give him a new name.\r\nThey will call his family “The House of the Unsandaled.”
passages.original: וְנִקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בֵּ֖ית חֲל֥וּץ הַנָּֽעַל׃ס

passages.text: If two men are fighting, and the wife of one steps in to rescue her husband from the one striking him, and she reaches out her hand and grabs his genitals, you are to cut off her hand. You must show her no pity.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel through Moses.
These laws teach justice and order.
If two men fight each other, they are brothers or fellow Israelites.
If the wife of one man comes near, she tries to save her husband from the man who is hitting him.
She reaches out her hand.
She grabs the other man’s private parts.
You must cut off her hand.
You must not show her any pity.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִנָּצ֨וּ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים יַחְדָּו֙ אִ֣ישׁ וְאָחִ֔יו וְקָֽרְבָה֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת הָֽאֶחָ֔ד לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־ אִישָׁ֖הּ מִיַּ֣ד מַכֵּ֑הוּ וְשָׁלְחָ֣ה יָדָ֔הּ וְהֶחֱזִ֖יקָה בִּמְבֻשָֽׁיו׃ וְקַצֹּתָ֖ה אֶת־ כַּפָּ֑הּ לֹ֥א תָח֖וֹס עֵינֶֽךָ׃ס

passages.text: You shall not have two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
passages.sermon:
God commands you.
You must not keep two different weights in your bag.
You must not have one heavy weight and one light weight.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ בְּכִֽיסְךָ֖ אֶ֣בֶן וָאָ֑בֶן גְּדוֹלָ֖ה וּקְטַנָּֽה׃ס

passages.text: You shall not have two differing measures in your house, one large and one small.
passages.sermon:
God commands you.
You must not keep two different measures in your house.
You must not have one large measure and one small measure.
You must not use unfair measures.
passages.original: לֹא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ בְּבֵיתְךָ֖ אֵיפָ֣ה וְאֵיפָ֑ה גְּדוֹלָ֖ה וּקְטַנָּֽה׃

passages.text: You must maintain accurate and honest weights and measures, so that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God is giving you a land to live in.
You must use accurate weights.
You must use honest weights.
You must use accurate measures.
You must use honest measures.
If you do this, you will live long in the land.
God gives you this land.
passages.original: אֶ֣בֶן שְׁלֵמָ֤ה וָצֶ֙דֶק֙ יִֽהְיֶה־ לָּ֔ךְ אֵיפָ֧ה שְׁלֵמָ֛ה וָצֶ֖דֶק יִֽהְיֶה־ לָּ֑ךְ לְמַ֙עַן֙ יַאֲרִ֣יכוּ יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: For everyone who behaves dishonestly in regard to these things is detestable to the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD your God hates dishonesty.
Anyone who acts dishonestly is detestable to Him.
This includes everyone who uses unfair measures or weights.
God rejects all who do wrong in these ways.
passages.original: כִּ֧י תוֹעֲבַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ כָּל־ עֹ֣שֵׂה אֵ֑לֶּה כֹּ֖ל עֹ֥שֵׂה עָֽוֶל׃פ

passages.text: Remember what the Amalekites did to you along your way from Egypt, how they met you on your journey when you were tired and weary, and they attacked all your stragglers; they had no fear of God.
passages.sermon:
The Amalekites attacked the Israelites.
The Israelites were traveling from Egypt.
The Amalekites met the Israelites on the road.
The Israelites were tired and weary.
The Amalekites attacked the stragglers at the back of the group.
The Amalekites did not fear God.
Remember what the Amalekites did to you.
passages.original: זָכ֕וֹר אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה לְךָ֖ עֲמָלֵ֑ק בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֥ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃ אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָֽרְךָ֜ בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ וַיְזַנֵּ֤ב בְּךָ֙ כָּל־ הַנֶּחֱשָׁלִ֣ים אַֽחַרֶ֔יךָ וְאַתָּ֖ה עָיֵ֣ף וְיָגֵ֑עַ וְלֹ֥א יָרֵ֖א אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: When the LORD your God gives you rest from the enemies around you in the land that He is giving you to possess as an inheritance, you are to blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget!
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD your God will give you rest.
He will give you rest from all your enemies around you.
He will do this in the land.
The LORD your God is giving you this land.
He is giving it to you as an inheritance.
You must blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.
Do not forget this.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֡ה בְּהָנִ֣יחַ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֣יךָ׀ לְ֠ךָ מִכָּל־ אֹ֨יְבֶ֜יךָ מִסָּבִ֗יב בָּאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְהוָֽה־ אֱ֠לֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵ֨ן לְךָ֤ נַחֲלָה֙ לְרִשְׁתָּ֔הּ תִּמְחֶה֙ אֶת־ זֵ֣כֶר עֲמָלֵ֔ק מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם לֹ֖א תִּשְׁכָּֽח׃פ
